goal: load_policy parses a new top-level [execution] mode (default local) onto WorkPolicy and raises a path-keyed PolicyError at load time when mode is distributed and store.backend is not postgres, while leaving all runtime scheduling/claim/lease behavior unchanged.

relevant: .flywheel/specs/00046-execution-mode-guard.md -- the acceptance criteria SC-1 through SC-8 this task satisfies, plus the Decisions Log (D-1..D-4) it must honor

packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_policy.py -- WorkPolicy, load_policy, _STORE_BACKENDS, and the existing _optional_* validators; add the [execution] mode field + parse + the cross-section guard here
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/tests/test_execution_mode.py -- the held-out oracle for this task; make it green, do not create or edit it (the grading harness owns it)
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/tests/test_policy.py -- pre-existing policy suite that must stay green; its store/source assertions are unchanged
references: packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_policy.py:971-975 -- mirror this cross-section fail-fast pattern (PolicyError keyed by policy_file, message naming both conditions) for the distributed+non-postgres guard

packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_policy.py -- _optional_store (~496) for the strict-validate / forward-compat (unknown keys ignored) validator shape to copy for [execution] mode
constraints: Default mode is local: a flywheel.toml with no [execution] table must resolve to local with no behavior change, so every existing config and test keeps passing.

The guard is the ONLY enforced effect of mode: it fires at load_policy time (after both mode and store.backend are resolved), raising PolicyError keyed by the policy file path and naming both the distributed mode and the store/backend. distributed+sqlite is the single rejected cell; local+sqlite, local+postgres, and distributed+postgres are all valid.

Strict-validate the mode value (an unrecognized mode raises a path-keyed PolicyError naming execution.mode and the value); ignore unknown KEYS under [execution], matching the _optional_* forward-compat convention.
Use PolicyError, not StoreConfigError, and do not add a new exception type; do not touch _store_factory.py or the store.backend default.
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done.
non_goals: Do not wire mode into scheduling, claim acquisition, lease renewal, or any multi-worker coordination path -- those are already always-on and mode must not gate them (spec D-4).
Do not validate Postgres reachability, DSN presence, pooler mode, or privileges -- only the mode/backend pairing is checked here.
Do not add any [execution] key other than mode, and do not introduce a third mode value.
Do not modify, create, or weaken files under packages/flywheel-orchestrator/tests/ (including the held-out oracle test_execution_mode.py); do not delete or soften any existing store/policy assertion.
edge_cases: An absent [execution] table resolves to mode=local (criterion #1).
distributed+postgres must succeed -- a blanket 'reject all distributed' implementation passes the distributed+sqlite rejection but fails this cell (criterion #4).
A present-but-unrecognized mode (e.g. 'cluster') fails fast with a path-keyed message naming execution.mode; it must NOT silently coerce to local (criterion #6).
An unknown key under [execution] (e.g. workers = 4) alongside a valid mode is ignored, not rejected (criterion #7).
